newsitem.title: CANADA: Patches of frost seen across Canada's Prairies.
newsitem.headline: Patches of frost seen across Canada's Prairies.

text.p: Frost was scattered across Canada's Prairies on Wednesday morning, Environment Canada said.
Grande Prairie, in Alberta's Peace River Valley, saw 0 Celsius (32 F) at 0300 CDT and fell to -1.0 Celsius at 0700 CDT at chest level, meteorologist Gerald Machnee said.
Ground temperatures can be 2.0 to 5.0 Celsius cooler.
Only 10 percent of Peace River Valley crops were combined by Monday, Alberta Agriculture said.
Pincher Creek, in the extreme southwest, saw -3.0 Celsius for four hours, Machnee said.
Lethbridge, in the southeast, saw -1.0 Celsius from midnight to 0400 CDT.
Southern Alberta's harvest was 80 to 90 percent complete by Monday, Alberta Agriculture said.

Kindersley, in west central Saskatchewan, saw -1.0 Celsius for two hours. Maple Creek, south of Kindersley, saw -2.0 for two hours. Val Marie, east of Maple Creek, saw 0 Celsius for two hours and Swift Current saw 0 Celsius for one hour.
The region's harvest was delayed in the past week as more than one inch of rain fell there. Harvest was 85 percent done around Maple Creek, Saskatchewan Agriculture said Monday.
West central Saskatchewan's harvest was 48 percent done.
Sprague, in southeast Manitoba, saw -1.0 Celsius at 0400 CDT, -3.0 Celsius at 0500 CDT and -4.0 Celsius at 0600 CDT.
Ninety percent of wheat, oats and barley were harvested in eastern Manitoba by Monday, Manitoba Agriculture said.
Alberta should see showers with highs of eight to 15 Celsius.
Saskatchewan should see showers in the south and highs near 10 Celsius.
Manitoba should see scattered rain with highs of 10 to 13 Celsius.
